title: After a BUILD INDEX, a duplicate-key insert raises <LIST ERROR>, which the duplicate check does not recognise
intended: `_write_txn.is_duplicate` (iris_vector_graph/_write_txn.py:46-49) treats a unique-key refusal as 'already there'.
observed: IRIS contract clause X-NOINDEX (round r6, scratch tables only): after BUILD INDEX a duplicate insert through DB-API raises DataError <LIST ERROR> instead of SQLCODE -119; is_duplicate matches only 'unique' or '-119'. Not reproduced on the product's own tables.
remedy: Recognise the <LIST ERROR> form in is_duplicate (or check the key explicitly) after index rebuilds.
notes: Candidate from the contract-extension lane; affects writers after the bulk loader's index rebuild or BUILD INDEX (modules 03, 08, 11).
